A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PBGD global-convergence study. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic representation-learning and data-hypercleaning experiments in Section 7, Figure 3, and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds stepsize sensitivity and baseline comparisons in Section 6 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The penalty objective, auxiliary-variable gradient estimation, Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel PBGD updates, and application models remain unchanged. Additional explanations and stronger theorem assumptions do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic two-layer linear representation-learning and noisy-label linear-regression hypercleaning tasks. Appendix H retains their data-generation distributions and corruption mechanism; the new comparisons use the existing representation-learning task.

E2.justification: F2SA and BOME, discussed but not experimentally compared in v1, become evaluated comparators against PBGD in v2 Figure 4(c–d). This introduces comparative evaluation where v1 reported only PBGD results.

E3.justification: v2 adds experiments sweeping the PBGD stepsizes α and β in Figure 4. The retained experiments keep the same sample counts, model dimensions, data generation, error metrics, and grid-search description in Appendix H.

E4.justification: Figure 4(a–b) adds stepsize sensitivity analysis, examining divergence and convergence speed as α and β vary. This extends the existing penalty-parameter sensitivity experiments without changing the application coverage.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run aggregation, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The additional curves retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds the first comparative convergence results for PBGD, F2SA, and BOME, alongside results showing stepsize-dependent divergence and slow convergence. These substantially extend the empirical findings beyond PBGD-only convergence demonstrations. The original Figure 3 curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 now requires the penalized lower-variable minimizer set to be independent of u in its blockwise case. Theorem 3 strengthens its diagonal-projector assumption to the concatenated training/validation matrix, supported by new Lemma 24. Example 1 changes sin(v) to 2sin(v), while the original example remains as Example 2; the revised Lemma 13 proof inconsistently mixes these coefficients.

C1.justification: The central PL conditions, PBGD convergence, and two application contributions remain. However, v2 Section 1.3 explicitly claims novelty for application-specific penalty-to-bilevel equivalence under local conditions, while removing v1's broader conclusion-level assertion of being the first global-convergence study for modern machine-learning applications.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive rationale for using linear models and interprets the new sensitivity and comparator results. It removes v1's explicit discussion of the missing general relationship between coupling structures and PL conditions, together with the proposed nonlinear extension through random features and neural tangent kernels.

D1.justification: The new Figure 4 legends disclose the tested α and β values. Appendix H otherwise preserves the existing generation recipes, metric approximations, and grid-search information; detailed configurations for the added baselines are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to single-level convergence work by Ma et al., Sun and Luo, and Ye and Du, plus a single-timescale bilevel method, and removes the limited-sample meta-learning survey. These support a more explicit justification of linear models, while the main positioning against prior bilevel methods remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially reorganized into labeled contributions and a new novelty/technical-challenges subsection. The former Section 4 becomes Section 3.3, the experimental discussion is rewritten around findings, and the conclusion is shortened. Citation style also changes throughout; most appendix proof text remains.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title block, typography, text width, and figure placement. Figure 1 is redrawn and expanded with a penalty-landscape panel, and Figure 4 adds sensitivity and comparator plots. Figures 2–3 retain their graphics, while the existing appendix figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons and sensitivity experiments provide useful evidence, and the stronger theorem assumptions make the guarantees more explicit. However, Appendix C.2 changes a previously consistent Lemma 13 proof to use 2sin(v) despite Example 2 retaining sin(v); its displayed gradient is no longer zero at the claimed point. Together with removed limitation discussion, this creates substantive tradeoffs between improved validation and reduced mathematical consistency, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
